precepts.text: Behold, I and the children whom the Lord hath given me are for signs and for wonders in Israel; the sign of Isaiah 7:14 was the child, not the virgin, and Isaiah counts himself and his children, never his wife.
precepts.point: Take counsel together and it shall come to nought, for God is with us, Immanuel: once the child was born, the two kings could not succeed against Judah.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
Isaiah had just told Ahaz, “the Lord himself shall give you a sign”. Then in chapter 8 the Lord has Isaiah write the name Maher-shalal-hash-baz, quick to the plunder, swift to the spoil, and Isaiah goes unto the prophetess, his wife, and “she conceived, and bare a son.” The child was named before he was conceived, the same way Gabriel named John and named Christ before they were conceived.

Then Isaiah says who the sign is: “Behold, I and the children whom the Lord hath given me are for signs and for wonders in Israel from the Lord of hosts, which dwelleth in mount Zion.” Behold who? I, Isaiah, and the children. Not his wife. He never counts the woman.

So the sign of Isaiah 7:14 was not the virgin; it was the child. The virgin birth was garbage. The birth of Isaiah's son was the sign that Ephraim and Syria banding together against Judah would fail. Before the child could cry “My father, and my mother,” the riches of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria were taken away before the king of Assyria. Assyria would pass through Judah and “reach even to the neck”, coming close to conquering but failing, because of Immanuel: “Take counsel together, and it shall come to nought; speak the word, and it shall not stand: for God is with us.” Once Isaiah's son was born, the two kings could not succeed against Judah.

precepts.point: Take counsel together and it shall come to nought, for God is with us, Immanuel: once the child was born, the two kings could not succeed against Judah.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
The Lord told Ezekiel to bear his stuff on his shoulders in their sight and carry it forth in the twilight, covering his face “that thou see not the ground: for I have set thee for a sign unto the house of Israel.” God made Ezekiel himself a sign unto the house of Israel.

Read on to verse 11 and Ezekiel is told to say it to Israel plainly: “Say, I am your sign: like as I have done, so shall it be done unto them: they shall remove and go into captivity.” What the prophet did, Israel would go through.

This lines up with Isaiah 8. When the Lord gives a sign, it is the man and the child he gives, not the woman. Isaiah and his children were signs and wonders in Israel, and Ezekiel was set for a sign to the house of Israel, which is why the sign of Isaiah 7:14 is the child born to Isaiah and the prophetess.

precepts.text: Thus Ezekiel is unto you a sign; according to all that he hath done shall ye do; the man is the sign, not his wife.
precepts.point: Take counsel together and it shall come to nought, for God is with us, Immanuel: once the child was born, the two kings could not succeed against Judah.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
“Thus Ezekiel is unto you a sign.” What is he? A sign. Not his wife: Ezekiel. “according to all that he hath done shall ye do: and when this cometh, ye shall know that I am the Lord God.”

The Lord told Ezekiel to eat dung, and what did we end up doing? Eating dung. He was a sign, and what he did came upon Israel.

Read on to verse 27: “thou shalt be a sign unto them; and they shall know that I am the Lord.” Again and again the man is the sign. So when Isaiah says “I and the children whom the Lord hath given me are for signs”, it fits the pattern of the prophets: the sign given to Ahaz was the child Isaiah's wife bare, Maher-shalal-hash-baz, not a virgin.

precepts.text: No sign shall be given but the sign of Jonas the prophet; as Jonas was a sign to the Ninevites, so shall the son of man be to this generation; men were always the signs, and even Hosea's marriage was his sign, never the woman by herself.
precepts.point: Take counsel together and it shall come to nought, for God is with us, Immanuel: once the child was born, the two kings could not succeed against Judah.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
When the people were gathered thick together, Christ said, “This is an evil generation: they seek a sign; and there shall no sign be given it, but the sign of Jonas the prophet.” Then: “For as Jonas was a sign unto the Ninevites, so shall also the Son of man be to this generation.”

Jonas was a sign. The Son of man was a sign. Men were always the signs. There is no scripture where the women were signs. Hosea was also a sign, and his marriage was a sign, but the woman by herself was never a sign.

That settles Isaiah 7 and 8. The Lord said he would give Ahaz a sign, and Isaiah tells us who it was: himself and the children the Lord gave him. The son born to Isaiah and the prophetess was the sign that God was with Judah, Immanuel, and that the two kings coming against Judah would come to nought.

precepts.text: Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples. The law is the seal.
precepts.point: The Song of Solomon is a metaphor: the whole book represents the Lord's relationship with his chosen people Israel. Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm. The heart is the mind. What is the seal? The law, the words of God.

note.label: 250 Years of Celebration 400 Years of Sweat Equity (Pt 2)

precepts.why:
Ezra said “the seal of Sion hath now lost her honour”. Here is what the seal of Zion is: “Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” Seal the law among my disciples. The law is the seal. The law is the seal.

That is what Solomon meant by “Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm”: the law of God set on the mind and bound on the arm, as Deuteronomy said to bind the words for a sign upon the hand. It is not the six-pointed star.

And it is the same seal the servants of God are sealed with in Revelation. So what is the seal we have to be sealed with? The law. The law. The law. There is nothing else to be said about it; if you keep pushing that star, that is your own vain opinion. Brothers and sisters, come on one accord and stop following the so-called white man and his lies.

precepts.point: God be thanked that ye were the servants of sin but have obeyed from the heart the doctrine delivered you: you understand your mission, as Bishop Kani said, the crown is already yours and it is for you to keep it on your head.

note.label: Eleutherophobia the Fear of Freedom

precepts.why:
“Know ye not, that to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are to whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness?” That is the million-dollar question: who do you give your service to? Money? The spirit of fornication? Alcoholism? The big-mouthed black woman that sleeps right next to you? Weakness as a man? Fear? Satan whispering that God can never use you because of your past? When you come into this truth and apply it, you are a new creature; old things are passed away.

“But God be thanked, that ye were the servants of sin, but ye have obeyed from the heart that form of doctrine which was delivered you.” What is that form of doctrine? “To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them.” The law and the testimony, the commandments and the testimony of Christ, is the doctrine delivered to us, and we obeyed it from the heart.

Thank God you understand your mission. You have your crown; it is already there, and it is for you to keep it on your head. You erase yourself out of the book of life; you are already ordained to get it. Will you hold on? “Here is the patience of the saints: here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus.”

Your opponent is not the brothers that look like you. First it is the man in the mirror, and sin is the op. Use this Bible to shoot down all sin that opposes you, and put your energy there. Many cannot function without an oppressor, because with freedom comes change and responsibility. Choose this day who your Lord is: sin unto death, or obedience to the law and the testimony unto righteousness.

precepts.point: He that endures to the end shall be saved. This gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness, and then shall the end come: that world is the 144,000, and when they are sealed the end comes.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
In Revelation 7 another angel ascends from the east “having the seal of the living God”, and the destruction is held back “till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.” What is the seal of the living God?

It is not the hexagram. Many of us thought so years ago when we were young. Isaiah says what it is: “Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” The seal of the living God is the law, bound up and sealed among his disciples. Pay attention, because if you blink you might miss it.

So the servants sealed in their foreheads are the ones with the law of God in their minds: “an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.” When they are sealed, the four winds are loosed and the end comes. That is why this gospel, the law and the testimony, has to be preached in all the world for a witness: to seal the 144,000 before the end.

precepts.text: Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples. That is what we bind the broken minds with: the laws of God, shown through our own lives as the example of why it is good to serve him.
precepts.point: Beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, trees of righteousness. They shall build the old wastes, strangers shall feed your flocks, and ye shall be named the priests of the Lord and eat the riches of the Gentiles.

note.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.why:
“The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me; because the Lord hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted.” He has chosen and set apart every man here, all the captains, to preach good tidings to the meek. But how do you bind up a person that is broken? The brokenhearted are broken in the mind: suffering the curses without knowing the will of God. We are set apart to bind them up. What do we bind them with?

“Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” We bind up the testimony and seal the law in the minds of the people, because they are brokenhearted and their minds are broken. That is what we are called to do: to bind them to the laws of God.

And we show them why it is good. Look at our lives as the example of what it means to serve God and why it is good to serve him. That means we have to be sincere about it. How do we tell the people to touch not the unclean thing and then not live it ourselves? The one who was profitable to many but not to himself will be punished accordingly, because he knew better.

So the good tidings we proclaim with the law are these: if we repent and keep God's laws in sincerity and endure to the end, he will deliver us, and we will rule again, as we were made in his image to rule.

precepts.text: To the law and to the testimony: that is the word, the engrafted word.
precepts.point: The same Paul who said no man is justified by the works of the law says not the hearers of the law are just before God but the doers of the law shall be justified. Was he schizophrenic? No; the law in Galatians is sacrifice, elaborated in Hebrews 7, 9 and 10, and the law here is the commandments, and faith comes first and the works follow.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
James says, “receive with meekness the engrafted word, which is able to save your souls.” What is the engrafted word? Isaiah answers it: “To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them.”

The law and the testimony is the word. So the word James says is able to save your soul, the word we must be doers of and not hearers only, is the law and the testimony: the commandments of God.

That is why Paul could say, “not the hearers of the law are just before God, but the doers of the law shall be justified.” The law he means there is the commandments, the engrafted word, not the sacrifices that Christ did away with.

So when the church says the law cannot save you, they are not speaking according to this word. Those who speak not according to the law and the testimony have no light in them. The word saves, Christ saves, and the doer of the word is the one justified.

note.label: Prophesy From Pain to Peace

precepts.why:
In Revelation 7 another angel ascends from the east “having the seal of the living God”, and he cries to the four angels, “Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.” What is the seal of the living God?

Isaiah answers: “Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” The seal is the law, the commandments. That is what the angel is looking for, and that is what he is doing: sealing the law among the disciples, the servants of God, in their foreheads, meaning in their minds.

The ones sealed are “an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.” When they are sealed with the law, the destruction is let loose and the end comes.

So the gospel of the kingdom preached in all the world for a witness is the law and the testimony going out to our people scattered among the nations, sealing them before the end. He that endures to the end, keeping it, the same shall be saved.

precepts.text: He shall be for a sanctuary, but for a stone of stumbling and a rock of offence to both the houses of Israel, a gin and a snare to the inhabitants of Jerusalem; many among them shall stumble, fall, be broken, snared and taken.
precepts.point: Behold, I lay in Zion a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone. Their covenant with death shall be disannulled. Today that covenant is the Christian pastors and Black politicians in bed with America, as the rulers then were in bed with Rome; and 'the report' they will not understand is Isaiah 53:1, that Christ is Messiah.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Isaiah 28 says they would “fall backward, and be broken, and snared, and taken.” Broken by what? By that stone of stumbling, that rock of offence. Isaiah 8 names it: “Sanctify the Lord of hosts himself; and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread. And he shall be for a sanctuary”. The same Lord shall be for a sanctuary, “but for a stone of stumbling and for a rock of offence to both the houses of Israel”, the southern and northern kingdom, “for a gin and for a snare to the inhabitants of Jerusalem.” A gin is a trap, a snare.

“And many among them shall stumble, and fall, and be broken, and be snared, and be taken.” Many among them means the rulers in Jerusalem. They stumbled, fell and were broken, as Psalm 69 said, and rejected the Messiah because they were evil, sinful and rebellious. That is who he is talking to: the elders, the builders, the rulers.

That stone is the “tried stone, a precious corner stone” Isaiah 28:16 lays in Zion, the same stone which the builders refused in Psalm 118. Peter quotes both Isaiah and David: “a stone of stumbling, and a rock of offence, even to them which stumble at the word, being disobedient: whereunto also they were appointed.” Them which stumble are the builders, the rulers, and the word is Christ, the same as the rock. Not all Israel refused him; the builders refused him. Appointed means they were predestined to reject him. Take good notes and tie these together: Isaiah 28, Isaiah 8, Psalm 118 and 1 Peter 2 are the same stone.

precepts.text: The Lord would be a stone of stumbling and a rock of offence to both the houses of Israel.
precepts.point: Within sixty-five years Ephraim would be broken, that it be not a people. That phrase is the key to the whole class.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

precepts.why:
In the days of Ahaz, Ephraim conspired with the Syrians to overthrow Judah: the Syro-Ephraimite war. Rezin was the king of Syria and Pekah the son of Remaliah was king of Ephraim, and their plan was to take Judah's land and set the son of Tabeal as king over it. Ahaz was weak and wicked, and his heart shook “as the trees of the wood are moved”. But the Lord said the counsel of Syria and Ephraim would not stand: “within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people.”

In Isaiah 8 the Lord brings “the king of Assyria, and all his glory” like a river over his banks. Assyria would rise up and conquer Ephraim, and also pass through Judah and take some portions of it, but not fully like Ephraim. “Take counsel together, and it shall come to nought” … “for God is with us.” Isaiah's sons were born as signs that Ephraim and Syria would be overthrown by Assyria and would not succeed against Judah.

So the Lord tells Isaiah not to fear their confederacy, and not to be like Ahaz, cowardly and weak: “Sanctify the Lord of hosts himself; and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread. And he shall be for a sanctuary; but for a stone of stumbling and for a rock of offence to both the houses of Israel.” It says both. The Lord speaks of one Israel as two houses: the house of Judah and the house of Ephraim, the southern kingdom and the northern kingdom. And that stone of stumbling is Christ.

He is “for a gin and for a snare to the inhabitants of Jerusalem”, a trap to both houses, but specifically to those in Jerusalem. “And many among them shall stumble, and fall, and be broken, and be snared, and be taken.” The context has not changed. Not only did Ephraim fall physically and spiritually; Judah fell physically and spiritually too, but worse, because they stumbled at that stone.

Hosea shows Ephraim's side. His daughter Lo-ruhamah, no mercy: “I will no more have mercy upon the house of Israel; but I will utterly take them away”, which is Assyria overthrowing Ephraim so that it be not a people. His son Lo-ammi: “for ye are not my people, and I will not be your God.” When you are not God's people and he is not your God, that makes you a Gentile, a heathen, a stranger, a non-Israelite. Judah read that and said, good, the hell with Ephraim, they are Gentiles, we don't deal with them anymore.

The rock ties it together. Moses said “He is the Rock, his work is perfect” … “a God of truth and without iniquity”, and “is not he thy father that hath bought thee?” That rock of Isaiah 8 is Christ, our God and our father, and the stone both houses of Israel stumbled over.

precepts.text: To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, there is no light in them.
precepts.point: Let them bring forth their witnesses; ye are my witnesses, saith the Lord. Israel, the stick of Judah and the stick of Ephraim, are his witnesses.

note.label: Judgement - the Testimony of the Two Witnesses

precepts.why:
“Let all the nations be gathered together, and let the people be assembled: who among them can declare this, and shew us former things? let them bring forth their witnesses.” Who can show the things from the past? The next verse answers: “Ye are my witnesses, saith the Lord, and my servant whom I have chosen.” God’s witnesses on this earth are the children of Israel, and the two sticks, the stick of Judah and the stick of Ephraim, the southern and northern kingdoms, are two witnesses also.
